title: Backfill fixture datasets + golden tests for Standard Cost Model computations (CI-integrated)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Create deterministic fixture datasets and golden tests for Standard Cost Model computations. Integrate into CI to prevent regressions in cost attribution, breakdown taxonomy, and what-if projections.

Why
Console and Optimize are converging on a single cost-model spec + API. We need a high-signal regression suite that catches:
- drift in per-request breakdown semantics (prefill vs decode, cache hits/misses)
- changes in overhead allocation rules
- rounding/unit normalization issues (tokens, ms, GPU-seconds)
- schema-version compatibility (unknown fields, defaulting, deprecations)

Scope (v1)
1) Fixture datasets
- Add a small set of curated JSON fixtures representing canonical scenarios.
- Fixtures must be stable, human-reviewable, and cover the most common production configurations.
- Fixtures should include both request-level inputs and expected outputs.

2) Golden tests
- Deterministic tests that compute cost breakdown outputs from fixture inputs and compare to expected (golden) outputs.
- Tests must run in CI on every PR touching:
  - cost-model schema package
  - cost-model service logic
  - telemetry input contract normalization
  - billing-hooks mapping to cost primitives

3) CI wiring
- Run golden tests in the normal unit test pipeline.
- Add a separate “golden refresh” workflow that is explicitly triggered (not automatic) and requires approval from owners (Platform + Finance partner) when goldens change.

Non-goals (v1)
- Full-scale replay of high-cardinality prod traffic (covered by the validation harness + drift job).
- Performance benchmarking (covered by perf suite / performance budget ticket).
- Establishing the billing system of record.

Proposed fixture taxonomy
A. Request-level, hosted (single request)
- chat.completions request
- typical token counts (prefill=~1k, decode=~200)
- no cache
- batch_size=1
- expected: breakdown with prefill/decode attribution + request overhead bucket

B. Request-level, hosted (cache hit)
- prefix cache hit rate ~80%
- expected: reduced prefill compute, explicit cache_credit/cached_prefill bucket per taxonomy

C. Dedicated deployment (reserved capacity)
- include deployment_mode=dedicated, sku metadata, and overhead allocation policy (capacity amortization bucket)
- expected: overhead allocation shown separately vs request-attributable compute

D. Quantization variant
- same workload expressed with quant_profile_id change
- expected: compute deltas and confidence metadata in what-if output (if present in v1 contract), with guardrails applied

E. Batching efficiency scenario
- batch_size>1 and effective batch efficiency <1.0 due to padding/fragmentation
- expected: batch efficiency factor applied to GPU-second attribution; decode/prefill remain consistent

Fixture format and location
- Add under monorepo path: cost-model/tests/fixtures/v1/
- Each scenario consists of:
  - input JSON: CostModelEstimateRequest (or library input struct)
  - expected JSON: CostModelEstimateResponse (including breakdown)
- Naming convention:
  - v1_hosted_simple.json
  - v1_hosted_cache_hit.json
  - v1_dedicated_capacity_amort.json
  - v1_quant_profile_int8.json
  - v1_batch_efficiency_padding.json

Determinism requirements
- No wall-clock reads, no live catalog lookups, no environment-dependent defaults.
- Any model catalog data required must be included as fixture-local “catalog snapshot” (or mocked/stubbed in test harness).
- All floating-point outputs must be rounded/normalized consistently (define precision per field, e.g., 1e-6 for GPU-seconds, cents to 1e-4).

Golden update policy
- Golden outputs should only change when:
  - schema semantics change (ADR approved) OR
  - bug fix to bring implementation in line with existing semantics
- Any golden change must include:
  - before/after diff
  - reason for change
  - approval comment from Platform (Ethan Park or Benji Okafor) + Finance partner (Rishi Malhotra or Laura Bennett delegate)

Acceptance criteria
- At least 5 fixtures added covering hosted, cache, dedicated, quantization, batching.
- Golden tests pass locally and in CI.
- CI prevents unreviewed golden changes (tests fail if outputs differ unless goldens are explicitly regenerated through the approved workflow).
- README in the fixtures directory describing:
  - how to run tests
  - how to add a new fixture
  - how to regenerate goldens
  - rounding rules

Implementation notes
- Prefer running tests against the shared cost-model library (not via network calls to service) for speed and determinism.
- Add one integration-style golden that hits the HTTP handler layer to ensure request/response serialization and defaulting behavior are stable.

Risks / gotchas
- Telemetry contract volatility: fixtures must pin a schema version and include explicit fields; avoid relying on “optional but usually present” telemetry.
- Floating point drift: define and enforce rounding; otherwise goldens will churn.
- Overhead allocation policy: ensure fixtures reflect the latest Finance-approved policy and taxonomy.

References
- Confluence: applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/cost-model-validation-harness.json (broader replay plan)
- ADR-022: cost breakdown taxonomy (prefill/decode, cache hits, batch efficiency, overhead allocation)
- Related PRs expected: schema package + service endpoints + drift monitoring
comments: 2026-01-23 (Leila Farouk): Drafted initial fixture list; proposing 5 scenarios (hosted simple, hosted cache-hit, dedicated amortized overhead, quant profile delta, batching efficiency). Need confirmation from Platform/Finance on overhead bucket naming for goldens.

2026-01-27 (Thomas Baird): Strong preference to run goldens against library-level compute to avoid handler-level defaulting differences in most tests. +1 on adding exactly one HTTP-level golden to cover serialization + bounds behavior.

2026-01-30 (Nadia Rahman): For cache-hit scenario, make sure we include both 'kv_prefix_cache' and 'prompt_cache' paths if they remain distinct in telemetry. If v1 is collapsing them, fixtures should follow the canonical collapsed field to avoid churn.

2026-02-06 (Rishi Malhotra): Finance review: overhead allocation must be explicitly labeled as 'overhead_allocated_usd' and separated from 'compute_attributable_usd'. Please also include a fixture that demonstrates rounding to 1/10,000 USD to match reporting windows.
2026-02-12 (Ethan Park): Approved adding a golden-refresh workflow with CODEOWNERS gating. Please ensure default behavior is 'fail on diff' in PR CI to avoid silent golden churn.

2026-02-18 (Leila Farouk): Implemented local harness and 3 fixtures; remaining: dedicated amortization + quant profile delta. Blocked on final field names from ENG-4822 schema review (version negotiation + rounding spec).
